settings.title: Gridlines
settings.description: Gridlines is a two-day conference on software for the energy transition, 19–20 November 2026 at Kraftwerk Berlin.

seo.description: Gridlines 2026: two days of talks and workshops on software for the energy transition, 19–20 November at Kraftwerk Berlin.
The full Gridlines 2026 schedule: keynotes, track talks, workshops and the Thursday party, 19–20 November in Berlin.
Meet the twelve Gridlines 2026 speakers from grid operators, wind farms, energy startups and open-source projects.
Gridlines 2026 passes from €120, early-bird prices until 16 October, and details on refunds, transfers, access and the venue.

values.tagline: The conference for people who write software for the energy transition. 19–20 November 2026 at Kraftwerk Berlin.

values.title: Software for a grid that runs on wind and sun
values.text: Two days of talks and hands-on workshops for the engineers, data scientists and product people building the energy transition, inside a former power station.

image.alt: The concrete main hall of Kraftwerk Berlin lit in red for the Gridlines opening keynote

values.title: Three tracks, one workshop day
values.intro: Every talk is about software running in production today: real systems, real numbers and no sales pitches.

image.alt: A speaker on the main stage in front of a slide showing grid frequency over one day

items.title: Main stage talks
items.text: Both keynotes and the strongest talk from each track, in the main hall, with live captions for every session.

items.title: Grid and flexibility
items.text: Congestion, balancing and demand response, and the code that runs them.

items.title: Forecasting and data
items.text: Weather, load and price forecasts, from notebooks to 15-minute production runs.

items.title: Homes and fleets
items.text: Heat pumps, batteries, EV charging and the apps people use to control them.

image.alt: Attendees with laptops at long tables during a hands-on workshop

items.title: Hands-on workshops on day two
items.text: Rooms of 40 seats, from OpenADR clients to forecasting with real smart-meter data. Pick your workshop when you book.

values.title: The energy software crowd, all in one hall
values.intro: Our fourth edition, and the first in a hall big enough for everyone on last year’s waiting list.

stats.label: Speakers who are women or non-binary

image.alt: The packed main hall during a keynote at Gridlines 2025, seen from the back row

values.title: Who takes the stage
values.intro: Twelve speakers from grid operators, wind farms, startups and open-source projects. Ines opens day one and Oluwaseun closes day two.

people.name: Ines Albrecht
people.bio: Opens day one with what 40,000 new heat pumps a month did to a distribution grid in northern Germany, and the software that kept it stable.

people.name: Marta Kowalczyk
people.bio: Runs the platform that bids 60,000 home batteries into local flexibility markets every 15 minutes.

people.name: Oluwaseun Adeyemi
people.bio: Closes day two with ten years of energy software, from pay-as-you-go solar in Lagos to virtual power plants in Europe.

values.quote: The person next to you at lunch runs the system you complained about in your talk. That only happens at Gridlines.
values.name: Grace Mwangi
values.role: Software engineer at Brightwatt, attendee in 2025

values.title: Our 2026 partners
values.text: Partners fund student passes, live captions and free recordings. Sponsorship packages start at €4,000.

values.title: Early-bird passes end 16 October
values.text: Save €200 on a pass that covers both days, every talk, a workshop seat, lunch and the Thursday party.

values.title: Two days, 46 sessions, one power station
values.text: Thursday is for talks on the main stage and in two track rooms. Friday is for hands-on workshops and the closing keynote. All times are Berlin time.

values.title: Hour by hour, both days
values.intro: Talks are 30 minutes including questions. The two track rooms run in parallel, and main stage sessions are recorded for ticket holders.

sessions.title: Doors open, coffee and badges
sessions.description: Breakfast from Berlin bakeries in the foyer. Bring a photo ID to pick up your badge.

sessions.title: The grid we planned for and the grid we got
sessions.speaker: Ines Albrecht, Nordwerk Netz
sessions.description: What 40,000 new heat pumps a month did to a distribution grid in northern Germany, and the software that kept it stable.

sessions.title: Forecasting solar output one cloud at a time
sessions.speaker: Rahul Iyer, Weatherline
sessions.description: Nowcasting with satellite images and 3,000 rooftop inverters, and why the last 15 minutes matter most.

sessions.title: Flexibility markets without spreadsheets
sessions.speaker: Marta Kowalczyk, Ampwise
sessions.description: How Ampwise bids 60,000 home batteries into local flexibility markets every 15 minutes, and settles every one of them.

sessions.title: Lunch
sessions.description: Long tables by topic: forecasting, markets, hardware and open source.

sessions.title: Who maintains the code that runs the grid?
sessions.speaker: Sanne de Vries, Tidewater Energy; Diego Navarro, OpenFlux Foundation; Elif Demir, Nordwerk Netz
sessions.description: Open source in a regulated industry: who reviews it, who pays for it and who gets the call at 3 am.

sessions.title: Charging 800 city buses overnight
sessions.speaker: Lars Eriksen, Voltpark
sessions.description: Scheduling depot charging for fleets in Oslo and Hamburg without upgrading a single substation.

sessions.title: Lightning talks
sessions.speaker: Eight attendees, five minutes each
sessions.description: Picked by attendee vote from 140 proposals. Sign-ups open in October.

sessions.title: Gridlines party
sessions.description: Food trucks, a hardware show-and-tell and a live DJ set in the main hall until 01:00.

sessions.title: Workshop: forecasting with your own meter data
sessions.speaker: Hana Kobayashi, Weatherline
sessions.description: Bring a laptop with Python 3.12. We provide a year of anonymized smart-meter data from 2,000 homes. 40 seats.

sessions.title: Workshop: build an OpenADR 3 client
sessions.speaker: Tomás Ferreira, Heatwell
sessions.description: Write a demand response client that a utility can send real signals to, and test it against our live server. 40 seats.

sessions.title: A digital twin for 30,000 kilometres of cable
sessions.speaker: Elif Demir, Nordwerk Netz
sessions.description: How a grid operator built a live model of its low-voltage network from meter data, and what it found.

sessions.title: Running a wind farm control room in the cloud
sessions.speaker: Jakob Lindqvist, Kestrel Wind
sessions.description: What it took to move monitoring for 400 turbines to the cloud, and what had to stay on site.

sessions.title: Lunch
sessions.description: Workshop leads join the tables to answer the questions you ran out of time for.

sessions.title: Dynamic tariffs people actually trust
sessions.speaker: Niamh O’Connor, Brightwatt
sessions.description: Results from 18 months of testing hourly prices with 9,000 households, and the app changes that made them stick.

sessions.title: Ten years of code for the energy transition
sessions.speaker: Oluwaseun Adeyemi, Sunloop
sessions.description: From pay-as-you-go solar in Lagos to virtual power plants in Europe: what scales and what never will.

sessions.title: Closing drinks
sessions.description: One last coffee or beer in the foyer before the trains home.

values.title: Then the party starts
values.body:
From 19:00 the main hall turns into the Gridlines party. It is included with every pass, and so is dinner.

  • Five Berlin food trucks, with vegan and halal options
  • A show-and-tell of home-built meters, inverters and chargers
  • A live set from the Berlin DJ collective Phasenwechsel until 01:00

image.alt: Attendees dancing under red stage lights in the main hall at the 2025 Gridlines party

values.title: Workshops have 40 seats per room
values.text: Pick yours when you book. Early-bird holders choose first.

values.title: Meet the 2026 speakers
values.text: Twelve speakers from grid operators, wind farms, startups and open-source projects, picked from 140 proposals by a committee of past attendees.

values.title: Twelve speakers, no sales pitches
values.intro: Every talk is about a system running in production today. Talk descriptions are on the schedule.

values.title: What makes a Gridlines talk
values.intro: Our program committee reads every proposal twice. These are the three things they look for.

items.title: Chosen by practitioners
items.text: Nine past attendees score every proposal with names and companies hidden.

items.title: Real systems, real numbers
items.text: Talks show code, data or incidents from production, including what went wrong.

items.title: No paid stage time
items.text: Sponsors cannot buy a talk. Product demos belong at the coffee bar, not on stage.

values.title: See all twelve live in Berlin
values.text: Early-bird passes are €390 until 16 October and include every talk, a workshop seat and the Thursday party.

values.title: One pass, both days
values.text: Every pass includes all talks, a workshop seat, lunch and coffee on both days, the Thursday party and the recordings. Prices include 19% German VAT.

values.title: Book early, pay less
values.intro: Standard passes cost €590 from 17 October. Need an invoice before you pay? Write to tickets@gridlines.example.

items.question: Can I get a refund?
items.answer: Yes. You get a full refund until 19 October and half the price back until 5 November. After that we cannot refund passes, but you can transfer yours to a colleague.

items.question: Can I transfer my pass to someone else?
items.answer: Yes, for free, until 18 November. Change the name with the link in your confirmation email. Team passes can change names as often as you need.

items.question: Is the venue accessible?
items.answer: The entrance, main hall and workshop rooms are step-free, with lifts between floors and accessible toilets. Every main stage session has live captions, and a quiet room is open on both days. Write to access@gridlines.example and we will plan your visit with you.

items.question: Do you offer free or reduced tickets?
items.answer: Yes. Besides the 100 student passes, our partners fund 60 free passes for people from groups under-represented in energy tech. Apply by 23 October.

items.question: Can my company pay by invoice?
items.answer: Yes. Choose invoice at checkout and add your company’s VAT ID. Invoices are due within 14 days and must be paid before 5 November.

items.question: Will the talks be recorded?
items.answer: Every main stage talk is recorded and shared with ticket holders a week after the conference. Recordings go public in January 2027.

values.title: A former power station
values.body:
Gridlines takes over Kraftwerk Berlin, a 1960s heating plant in Mitte with a main hall of raw concrete and steel, ten minutes from Alexanderplatz.

  • Address: Köpenicker Straße 70, 10179 Berlin
  • Underground: U8 to Heinrich-Heine-Straße, then five minutes on foot
  • S-Bahn: Jannowitzbrücke, then ten minutes on foot
  • Hotels: partner rates near the venue until 16 October, linked in your booking email
